housing.summary: Helsinki has a competitive rental market. Most landlords require proof of income and ID. Average 1BR in city centre ~€1,100–1,400/month. Deposits typically 1–2 months' rent. Key portals: Vuokraovi.com, Oikotie Asunnot.

banking.summary: Major banks: Nordea, OP (Osuuspankki), Danske Bank, S-Pankki. Non-residents can open accounts with passport and Finnish personal identity code (henkilötunnus). Some banks require proof of address. Digital banks (Holvi, Revolut) available as alternatives.

schools.summary: Helsinki has Finnish-medium and Swedish-medium public schools (free), plus international schools (fee-paying). Key international options: Helsinki International School, European School Helsinki, Deutsche Schule Helsinki. Curricula: Finnish national, IB, German.

legal_admin.summary: EU/EEA citizens must register with the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV) to obtain a Finnish personal identity code (henkilötunnus). Non-EU nationals need a residence permit from Migri (Finnish Immigration Service) before registering. Registration at local Maistraatti/DVV office.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register at DVV (Digital and Population Data Services Agency) to obtain henkilötunnus. EU/EEA: bring passport, employment contract or study confirmation. Non-EU: obtain residence permit from Migri first.

tax_finance.summary: Tax ID is the henkilötunnus (Finnish personal identity code). Employees receive a tax card (verokortti) from the Finnish Tax Administration (Vero). Register via OmaVero portal. Employer withholds income tax at source based on the tax card.
tax_finance.tax_id_name: Henkilötunnus (Finnish personal identity code) + verokortti (tax card)

transport.summary: HSL (Helsingin seudun liikenne) operates metro, tram, bus, and commuter rail. Monthly regional pass (AB zones, city + Espoo): ~€59.40/month. Driving licence: EU licences valid; non-EU licences from most countries valid for 2 years after registering, then must exchange via Traficom.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences remain valid. Non-EU licences valid for up to 2 years after gaining permanent residence; exchange via Traficom (Finnish Transport and Communications Agency).

healthcare_registration.summary: EU/EEA employees contribute to KELA (Kansaneläkelaitos) via employer payroll. Register with KELA to receive a KELA card granting access to public health services. GP services via public health centres (terveysasema) or occupational health (työterveyshuolto) through employer.
healthcare_registration.authority: KELA (Kansaneläkelaitos — Social Insurance Institution of Finland)
steps: Register at DVV to get henkilötunnus
Apply for KELA card online or at KELA office
Register at local terveysasema (health centre) in your district
